Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): Hey team—we're seeing deprovisioned users reappear in Redwood after a few hours. We deleted them from Okta (pushed via SCIM) but they come back with status ACTIVE.
Maya Patel (Customer Success): Sorry you're hitting this Lina. Can you share a recent user id and the API responses you saw when you deleted them?
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): example user id: 5f3a2c9b-9d1a-4f6a-8e2d-1234567890ab. Okta shows DELETE success. Our logs show: HTTP 200 OK from Redwood SCIM endpoint with body: `{
  "id": "5f3a2c9b-9d1a-4f6a-8e2d-1234567890ab",
  "active": false,
  "meta": { "resourceType": "User", "location": "https://api.redwood.ai/scim/v2/Users/5f3a..." }
}`
Maya Patel (Customer Success): Thanks. Can you paste the SCIM webhook / audit payload from the same window?
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): Here's the payload Okta sent (trimmed):
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
  "id": "5f3a2c9b-9d1a-4f6a-8e2d-1234567890ab",
  "userName": "l.cheng@example.com",
  "active": false,
  "groups": ["eng-team","contractors"]
}
```
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): Quick note — if Okta sends a DELETE vs a modify with active=false it can hit different code paths. Lina, do you know if Okta performs a full DELETE or a profile update?
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): It's the Okta "deactivate user" flow which sometimes issues a PATCH (active=false) and sometimes a DELETE depending on the provisioning policy.
Maya Patel (Customer Success): Owen / Jin, assigning to you. Repro steps: 1) Okta deactivate -> sends PATCH active=false 2) Redwood returns 200 3) User is marked inactive 4) After ~3 hours user becomes ACTIVE again and groups reappear.
Jin Park (SRE): Noted. Lina, do you have the event timestamps for when the user flips back? Any idea if there are re-provisioning events from another identity source?
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): Timestamp: 2025-09-02T14:13:02Z (deactivate), back to active at 2025-09-02T17:21:35Z. No other IDP configured. Only Okta.
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): I'm seeing a pattern in other customers — group-to-role mapping sync runs every 2 hours and will create users if group membership mapping expects them. Hypothesis: a mapping rule that maps group membership to role with a "ensure user" flag may be creating users when groups are reconciled.
Maya Patel (Customer Success): That fits the timeline. Lina, can you confirm if the groups in Okta still contain the user after deactivate?
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): Deactivated users are still in some groups (our policy keeps them for record). They expect deprovisioning to remove access in Redwood.
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): Ok — here's likely root cause: our SCIM engine has two reconciliation passes: membership-reconcile (every 2h) and lifecycle-reconcile (near-real-time for active flag). If membership-reconcile sees user listed in a group that maps to a Redwood role with createOnMembership=true, it will recreate or reactivate the user even if lifecycle set active=false earlier. There's a precedence bug where createOnMembership overrides explicit lifecycle deletes.
Jin Park (SRE): Repro steps I ran in staging:
1) Create user U in Okta -> push to Redwood (active=true)
2) Okta PATCH active=false -> Redwood marks inactive (200)
3) Keep U in Okta group G that maps to Redwood role with createOnMembership=true
4) membership-reconcile job runs -> Redwood sends POST /internal/users with the same email -> user becomes active again
Repro confirmed.
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): Example of internal call we see in logs:
```http
POST /internal/users HTTP/1.1
Host: internal-api:8080
Content-Type: application/json

{ "email": "l.cheng@example.com", "source": "scim-membership-sync", "force_activate": true }
```
SCIM Bot: [info] membership-reconcile job started (job_id=mr-20250902-17)
SCIM Bot: [info] membership-reconcile created user 5f3a2c9b-9d1a... via scim-membership-sync
Rajiv Menon (Product): This precedence is by design historically (teams wanted membership to ensure access), but obviously it's surprising when customers rely on lifecycle deprovisioning. We need to add a mapping precedence option and a quick mitigation.
Maya Patel (Customer Success): Lina — sorry for the disruption. Temporary mitigation: remove deactivated users from Okta groups or change mapping in Redwood Console to not auto-create on membership. Owen/Jin — can we offer a server-side feature-flag to prefer lifecycle over membership for this customer?
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): Yes. I can push a feature-flag (scim.precedence.lifecycle_over_membership = true) scoped to the customer org id. That will make lifecycle deactivations final until admin re-adds user to group. It requires a config toggle and small guard in membership-reconcile to respect lifecycle flags.
Jin Park (SRE): We'll need to deploy to staging + canary the flag. Low-risk change but touches reconciliation job. Timeline: patch + test => ~6 hours, deploy to canary => 1h, monitor 24h.
Maya Patel (Customer Success): Lina — would you like us to apply the feature-flag to your org now and monitor?
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): Yes please, that'd be great. Also can you provide a log snippet to show the create-on-membership event so we can audit?
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): Pasted anonymized log lines for audit: `membership-reconcile: user_create_attempt email=l.cheng@example.com org=redwood-acme reason=group_map:eng-team create_on_membership=true`
Maya Patel (Customer Success): Action items:
- Owen: prepare and apply feature-flag to org redwood-acme (ETA 6h)
- Jin: deploy to canary and monitor membership-reconcile metrics (ETA 8h)
- Maya: follow up with Lina and confirm groups removed or flag applied
- Rajiv: prioritize mapping precedence as product change to expose in Console (spec + UX)
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): One more note — longer-term fix is to add explicit mapping attributes: `create_on_membership`, `reactivate_on_membership`, and `lifecycle_precedence` with clear semantics. I'll draft the API changes.
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): Thanks everyone. For visibility — can you confirm what the SCIM response should look like for a deactivate that we can rely on?
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): For deprovisioning we accept either DELETE or PATCH active=false. We return 200/204 on success. With the feature-flag applied, a PATCH active=false will ensure user stays inactive even if group membership remains.
Jin Park (SRE): I'll add monitors: any reactivation events where `source=scim-membership-sync` will alert on customer orgs with the flag unset.
Maya Patel (Customer Success): I'll DM Lina when the flag is applied and check in 24 hours. Thanks team. :heart:
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): Appreciate it — looking forward to the fix.
Rajiv Menon (Product): Moving to backlog item PROD-1379 to add explicit precedence controls in Console. I'll loop in design/tx.
SCIM Bot: [info] feature-flag scim.precedence.lifecycle_over_membership applied to org redwood-acme by o.reed
Owen Reed (Identity Eng): Flag live in canary, applying to redwood-acme now.
Jin Park (SRE): Canary looks good — no errors, membership-reconcile respects lifecycle. Monitoring enabled.
Maya Patel (Customer Success): Lina — flag is on. I'll check in tomorrow morning.
Lina Cheng (Okta Admin - customer): Confirmed — no reactivations in the last 6h. Thank you!
Maya Patel (Customer Success): Closing loop once 24h stable. Thanks everyone.
